statement: EMIB-T substrate mass production is expected in 2027 with initial yields targeted at 50%, while Unimicron says full-scale mass production is unlikely before 2027 and that avoiding the interposer could create a cost gap of as much as 40-50% versus CoWoS.
why: A 50% starting yield and a 2027 timeline mean the new packaging capacity arrives slowly, while a 40-50% cost advantage is the pull that would make customers switch once it does.

impact.mechanism: Low initial substrate yields delay meaningful capacity relief into 2027, while a large cost gap versus interposer-based packaging pulls accelerator programs toward the alternative platform over multiple generations.

evidence.excerpt: substrate mass production expected "next year" (2027), with initial yields targeted at 50%

confidence.basis: Supply-chain figures attributed to named substrate makers via trade press; targets and expectations rather than achieved results.

dispersion: Timeline and cost stated as ranges: 2027 mass production with 50% initial yield; cost gap of 40-50%.
